outcome: No proof, disproof, counterexample, or narrowing of Agrawal's conjecture has appeared since 26 January 2024; the last substantive activity (the Primaboinca distributed search and the Pomerance-Lenstra heuristic) predates the window by years.
summary: I searched extensively for any post-26-January-2024 activity on Agrawal's conjecture (that (X-1)^n ≡ X^n - 1 mod (n, X^r-1) implies n is prime or n^2 ≡ 1 mod r) and found none. The current (2026) Wikipedia article on Agrawal's conjecture and on the AKS primality test both describe the same state of knowledge that existed before the window: computational verification for small ranges, the Primaboinca BOINC project (2010-2020, ended 31 May 2020, searched 10^10 < n < 10^17, no counterexample found), Popovych's modified conjecture (2008/2009), and the Pomerance-Lenstra heuristic argument that counterexamples should have positive density and are 'probably' infinite (this heuristic itself predates 2024 by roughly two decades and is unchanged in any of the sources I read). I also checked arXiv listings and general web search for any 2024-2026 preprints mentioning 'Agrawal's conjecture', 'cyclotomic AKS', or related search terms, and found only unrelated cyclotomic-polynomial papers with no connection to this conjecture. A 'Grokipedia' AI-generated encyclopedia page also exists on this topic but likewise reports no developments after January 2024 and is not itself a primary source. No lab, paper, or blog credits an AI system with any work on this conjecture. The Pomerance-Lenstra heuristic (an existence/infinitude-type argument about counterexamples) is not itself a resolution per §3.1 — 'are there infinitely many counterexamples' is not advanced by anything found here, and in any case it predates the window entirely. This is a clean 'nothing happened' case: the conjecture is exactly where it was in January 2024, with no narrowing, no case settled, and no AI involvement of any kind.
competing_reading: None found. The only mild wrinkle is that the Wikipedia article and AKS primality test article have presumably been edited since January 2024 (both were fetched as they exist in 2026), but their content shows no new mathematical claims postdating the frozen revision — they restate the same 2001-2020 facts. There is no plausible alternative classification other than open/no_change_found.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement (i) exhibiting an explicit n, r counterexample to the cyclotomic congruence, (ii) proving the conjecture true, (iii) proving/disproving Popovych's modified variant, or (iv) reporting a renewed/extended distributed or targeted computational search beyond the Primaboinca range (10^17) that either found a counterexample or extended the verified range — any of these dated after 26 January 2024 would change this record.
